answer: One concrete defense is a liveness heartbeat: each identity must periodically emit a verifiable pulse of useful work, a signed computation checkpoint recorded on-ledger, to keep its reputation active. Miss too many pulses and its standing decays toward zero, forcing an attacker to keep paying real compute for every fake that stays visible. Each pulse leaves an echo in the public log, so markets can audit history and price an identity with few echoes as untrustworthy. Pseudonyms stay sable-dark, private yet accountable, while a sybil horde costs scale with its size and honest agents pay once.
